claims.text: The initial material is a W–Cu composite containing discrete W particles or interconnected W ligaments in a Cu matrix.
The untreated W–Cu composite develops phase separation and interfacial voids under the stated service conditions.
A thin refractory high-entropy-alloy interlayer can be deposited or incorporated between W and Cu.
(CrFeTiTa)70W30 is a candidate refractory high-entropy alloy for the interlayer.
Temperatures of approximately 1100–1500 °C are applicable processing or service boundaries for the proposed intervention.
The proposed intervention is applicable under high-fluence ion irradiation.
The RHEA interlayer provides a graded structural bond at the W–Cu interface.
The RHEA interlayer reduces thermal-expansion mismatch between W and Cu.
The RHEA interlayer acts as a diffusion barrier.
Chemical and structural compatibility of the RHEA with W and Cu minimizes W–Cu interdiffusion.
Reduced interdiffusion suppresses void nucleation at the W–Cu interface.
The RHEA interlayer impedes phase separation in the W–Cu composite.
Suppressing voids and phase separation maintains a more coherent W–Cu interface.
Maintaining a coherent interface preserves thermal conductivity during thermal cycling and irradiation.
The RHEA-interlayered composite will have better interfacial integrity than an untreated W–Cu composite under matched thermal and irradiation conditions.
The RHEA-interlayered composite will retain higher thermal conductivity than an untreated W–Cu composite under matched thermal and irradiation conditions.
Void formation and phase separation reduce the thermal conductivity of the untreated composite.
The intervention is expected to remain effective up to approximately 1500 °C in high-fluence irradiation environments.
